h1: Freestanding bath installation in Stoke Poges

hero.intro: Stoke Poges is a village of large plots and substantial houses, with Stoke Park's golf and country club giving the area its best-known identity, and the housing around it ranging from older period detached homes to more recent executive-style builds, many set well back on sizeable gardens. That scale generally gives us more room to manoeuvre on bathroom layout than a smaller property allows — including positioning a freestanding bath exactly where a client wants it, rather than where the existing pipework happens to be. We handle the positioning, the waste and overflow routing, and the floor loading check as one job.

sections.heading: Positioning a freestanding bath where you actually want it
sections.body: One of the main reasons clients choose a freestanding bath is to make it a feature of the room rather than tucking it against a wall — which is exactly where Stoke Poges' larger properties help. A bath positioned away from every wall needs its waste, overflow and filler supply running to it rather than relying on existing pipe runs nearby, so the room has to have the space to accommodate that pipework discreetly, usually beneath the bath itself. On the larger period and executive-style homes typical of the area, we can usually agree a position at survey stage and build the plumbing route to suit it, rather than the position being dictated by where an old bath used to sit.

sections.heading: Waste, overflow and floor loading
sections.body: A freestanding bath carries its waste, overflow and filler supply to wherever it's positioned, which in practice means routing pipework either under a shallow raised plinth built around the bath's base, or through a section of floor opened up and reinstated once the pipe run is in. Alongside that, the floor itself needs checking: a full freestanding bath with someone in it can weigh well over 200kg, which is a real point load that has to sit on joists capable of carrying it, or be spread across a wider bearing area if not. We check both at survey, before any pricing or scheduling is finalised.

sections.heading: What Stoke Poges' housing means for this job
sections.body: The older period detached homes in and around Stoke Poges tend to have suspended timber floors, which is generally workable for a freestanding bath but does mean confirming joist direction and spacing before committing to a position — running new waste pipe across the joists rather than along them needs doing properly. The more recent executive-style builds, often set well back on larger gardens, tend to offer wider room dimensions and more flexibility on where the bath and its plumbing can go. In both cases, the generous plot sizes common across the village mean relocating a waste run, or even adding a second bathroom off a principal bedroom with its own freestanding bath, rarely runs into the structural constraints a terraced house would present.

sections.heading: How the job runs
sections.body: We start with the £125 paid survey to check the floor structure, agree where the bath will sit, and plan the waste and overflow route around it. From there: strip-out of the old suite, first-fix plumbing to the new position, any floor reinforcement or plinth work identified at survey, tiling around the fixed pipework, then the bath goes in, is connected, and is snagged and signed off. You source the bath and fittings; we do everything from strip-out to final connection, from £3,500. Call or WhatsApp 07399 651836 to arrange a survey.

faqs.q: Can a freestanding bath go anywhere in the room?
faqs.a: In principle yes, but the waste, overflow and filler all need a practical route to reach it, and the floor underneath needs to be able to carry the weight once it's full. We assess both at survey before confirming a position with you.

faqs.q: Do older Stoke Poges properties need extra work for a freestanding bath?
faqs.a: Often some, yes — period homes with suspended timber floors need joist spacing and direction checked before we commit to a bath position, since the waste pipe has to cross or run alongside the joists properly. It's a standard part of the survey, not an unusual extra.

faqs.q: Can you add a freestanding bath to a principal bedroom's ensuite?
faqs.a: Yes, this is a common request on the larger properties typical of Stoke Poges, where there's often enough space off a principal bedroom to add or upgrade an ensuite with a freestanding bath as the centrepiece.

faqs.q: Do you supply the bath and fittings?
faqs.a: No, we're a fit-only installer — you choose and buy the bath, filler, waste and overflow fittings. We carry out the strip-out, first-fix, tiling, plumbing and snagging.

faqs.q: How much does a freestanding bath installation cost in Stoke Poges?
faqs.a: Our installs start from £3,500. The final figure depends on the extent of floor work and waste routing required, which we confirm after the paid survey.
